sex-age.summary: How a painted person reads as female or male, child, adult or old. Ambiguity reads male, so a woman needs positive feminine cues; several moderate cues agreeing beat one exaggerated cue. At thumbnail size only hair, outline (jaw, neck, shoulder-hip, waist), facial contrast and skin colour survive.

male_bias.value: ambiguous bodies and faces are categorised as male, and faster; feminine cues must be present, not just masculine ones absent
male_bias.source: Johnson, Iida and Tassinary 2012, Proc R Soc B (PubMed 23075835)

face_accuracy.value: hair hidden: humans 96%; 12 full-face distances 85%; 16 2-D+3-D measures 94%

face_feature_rank_isolated.value: brows+eyes > brows > eyes > jaw > chin > nose+mouth > mouth; nose alone carries nothing

facial_contrast.value: higher eye/lip-to-skin luminance contrast reads female, lower reads male; can flip an androgynous face; strongest face cue that survives blur
facial_contrast.source: Russell 2009, Perception; 'strongest at blur' is judgement

skin_colour.value: redder skin reads male, greener-yellower female; redder lips read female; beard zone darker in men
skin_colour.source: Dupuis-Roy et al. 2009 (ScienceDaily); Dupuis-Roy and Gosselin 2015 (Medical Xpress)

brow_to_eye.value: larger lid band under the brow in women; important, but less than eye and mouth luminance

fwhr.value: not sexually dimorphic: do not use

lower_face.value: lower third 64.3 mm women vs 72.6 mm men; lower-face/face height and cheekbone prominence differ strongly
lower_face.source: Farkas via face.md section 9; Lefevre et al. 2012

hair.value: most dominant single social cue; can override the face early in perception

thumbnail.value: hair masked: 6.5% error at 80x40 px, 31% at 21x12 px

whr.value: women about 0.72, men about 0.89, boundary about 0.80; body shape outweighs motion

shoulders.value: biacromial 41.1 cm men, 36.7 cm women (ratio 1.12); hip:shoulder circumference 1:1.03 women, 1:1.18 men

gait.value: point-light walkers: humans about 66% correct, ideal observer on shoulder/(shoulder+hip) about 79%; hip/shoulder sway disputed
gait.source: Pollick lecture (Pollick et al. 2005; Cutting et al. 1978; Mather and Murdoch 1994)

muscle_fat.value: men about 78% more arm muscle, 50% more thigh muscle, 90% more upper-body strength; body fat 23.2% men, 33.9% women

posture_cultural.value: head cant, bashful knee bend, feminine touch, licensed withdrawal are display stereotypes, not anatomy: never use them to signal sex

age_skin.value: skin topography explains much of perceived age; uneven colour looks older
age_skin.source: Fink and Matts 2008; Fink, Grammer and Matts 2006

age_contrast.value: facial contrast falls with age; lower contrast reads older (and more male)

grey_hair.value: 45-65: 74% have some grey, mean 27%; at 50 only 6-23% are half grey

head_heights.value: 4 at birth, about 5 at 2, 5.5-6 at 5-9, 6.5-7 adolescent, 7.5 adult, less when stooped in old age

face_full_size.source: Brown and Perrett 1993; Bruce et al. 1993; Russell 2009; Lefevre 2012; weights are judgement from these rankings

thumbnail_survive: facial contrast as dark eye band and mouth vs skin
cue_weights.thumbnail_source: Moghaddam and Yang 2000; Sinha et al. 2006; the split is judgement

woman: Eye darks and lips stand clearly off a lighter skin; no grey beard zone
Jaw narrows to a small chin; outline rounded, not square at the jaw angle
Brow a thin higher arch with light on the lid band beneath
Neck slimmer than the jaw, long, on sloping shoulders
Waist in, hips out (WHR well under 0.8); shoulders no wider than hips
Smooth continuous forms, no separate muscle blocks
With short or hidden hair, the above still reads alone
man: Lower facial contrast; darker, redder skin with cooler beard zone
Wide jaw angle, broad chin; heavy straight brow low over a shadowed eye
Thick neck, trapezius high; Adam's apple in profile
Wedge: shoulders clearly wider than hips, little waist (WHR about 0.9)
Separate arm and shoulder masses, crisper plane breaks
child: Small low face under a large cranium; eyes below the half line, big eyes, small nose and chin, full cheeks
Short thick limbs; body midpoint near the navel
Smooth even rosy skin, no facial plane breaks
Sex, if it matters, from hair and clothes
old: Stoop, forward head, shorter neck, arms hanging lower
Grey or white thinner hair; temple or crown recession in men
Hollow temples, dropped cheek, jowl breaking the jawline, deep nasolabial folds as value shapes
Lower facial contrast, uneven skin colour
Old woman: keep one or two female cues strong (neck, jaw outline, hair, body line)

avoid: a 'neutral' woman with no positive feminine cues (reads male)
same skin value and feature darks for woman and man
grey beard zone or hard jaw shadow on a woman
sex carried only by hair and clothing
stereotyped poses (head cant, knee bend) as the sex signal
ageing by drawn lines on a young structure
over-ageing a 40-year-old with deep folds and grey
using face width-to-height ratio as a sex cue
